figures.finding: Salary income tax (IRSA) is levied monthly at 0% to MGA 350,000, 5% to 400,000, 10% to 500,000, 15% to 600,000, 20% to 4,000,000 and, from the 2026 finance law, 25% above 4,000,000 (minimum MGA 3,000); an individual business with turnover under MGA 400 million pays a 5% synthetic tax on turnover instead of income tax.
figures.applies: 2026 (Loi de finances 2026, art. 01.03.16; the amending finance law of July 2026 does not touch it).

sources.said: Article 01.03.16.- Modifier la rédaction du A. Droit commun de cet article comme suit : « A. Droit commun - jusqu’à Ar 350 000 : 0p.100 ; - tranche de revenu de Ar 350 001 à Ar 400 000 : 5p.100 ; - tranche de revenu de Ar 400 001 à Ar 500 000 : 10p.100 ; … - tranche de revenu de Ar 500 001 à Ar 600 000 : 15p.100 ; - tranche de revenu de Ar 600 001 à Ar 4 000 000 : 20p. 100 ; - tranche de revenu supérieure à Ar 4 000 000 : 25p. 100. »

Income range up to 350,000 Malagasy ariary (MGA): 0% Income range from MGA 350,001 to MGA 400,000: 5% Income range from MGA 400,001 to MGA 500,000: 10% Income range from MGA 500,001 to MGA 600,000: 15% Income range above MGA 600,000: 20%
An individual business having an annual turnover of less than MGA 400 million is subject to IR at a rate of 5% (with a possible reduction of 70%) of the annual turnover, called 'synthetic tax'.

figures.finding: IRSA is withheld monthly and paid before the 15th; a small business's return is due 31 March.

sources.said: Payment of IRSA must be done before the 15th day of each month.
Small business income tax returns must be filed with the tax office by 31 March of each year.

figures.finding: The employer pays 13% pension (CNaPS) and 5% health, the employee 1% and 1%, each capped at eight times the legal minimum wage a month; the employer also pays 1% FNFP.

value.cap: 8 x legal minimum wage per month

sources.said: Employers contribute to the National Pensions Fund at 13% of cash remuneration, up to a monthly maximum amount of 13% of eight times the legal minimum salary, per employee.
Employees contribute to the National Pensions Fund at 1%, subject to a monthly maximum amount of 1% of eight times the legal minimum salary.

figures.finding: Salary tax and social contributions are withheld monthly by the employer; purchases of services from a non-registered supplier bear 5% withholding.

sources.said: The tax on salary and all statutory social contributions are withheld monthly by the employer, who is responsible for tax filing and payment.
Purchases of goods and services from non-registered suppliers by a registered supplier are subject to WHT at a rate of 5%

figures.finding: Royalties, service fees and any income earned by a foreign supplier bear 10% withholding.

sources.said: Management fees, royalties, technical and assistance fees, licence fees, equipment rental fees, and any income realised by foreign suppliers is subject to WHT at a rate of 10%.

figures.finding: VAT is 20%; a person whose turnover or income reaches MGA 400 million (or who opts for it) is under the real regime, which brings both income tax and VAT; from MGA 200 million he may opt for income tax without VAT, and below that he pays the synthetic tax and no VAT.

sources.said: dont le chiffre d’affaires et/ou revenus est supérieur ou égal à Ar 400 000 000 ou - dont le chiffre d’affaires et/ou revenus est supérieur ou égal à Ar 200 000 000, optant pour l’imposition à l’Impôt sur les revenus ; ou par celles optant pour le régime du réel. Le régime du réel implique la soumission à la fois à l’Impôt sur le revenu et à la taxe sur la valeur ajoutée.
